## About

This repository contains the official InfluxDB image for Azure Linux.

### What is Azure Linux?

Azure Linux is a Linux distribution for Microsoft’s cloud infrastructure and edge products and services. Azure Linux is designed to provide a consistent platform for these devices and services and will enhance Microsoft’s ability to stay current on Linux updates.  

To learn more about Azure Linux, refer to our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/microsoft/azurelinux/).

### What is InfluxDB?

InfluxDB is a time series database built from the ground up to handle high write and query loads. InfluxDB is meant to be used as a backing store for any use case involving large amounts of timestamped data, including DevOps monitoring, application metrics, IoT sensor data, and real-time analytics.

See: [wikipedia.org/wiki/InfluxDB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/InfluxDB)

## Featured tags

- `2`

The featured tags are multi-architecture tags (i.e., `x86-64` and `aarch64`) that refer to the latest version of the image. Additional tags that are specific to influxdb version, Azure Linux build, or architecture can be found in the Tags section.

## Configuration

InfluxDB can be configured using a mix of a config file, environment variables, and CLI options. The easiest way is to follow [`Automated Database Setup`](#automated-database-setup), at the end of it the server container will keep running named `influx-server`. If you need to start the container that is already configured, refer to [`Start a InfluxDB instance`](#start-an-influxdb-instance). If you need to get a config file for the InfluxDB, once your database is configured and is running with container name `influx-server`, you can use this command to get it using Influx CLI shipped with the container:

    docker exec influx-server influx server-config > config.yml

For more configuration options refer to [Configuration Page](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.6/reference/config-options/)

### Automated Database Setup
The InfluxDB image contains some extra functionality to automatically bootstrap the system. This functionality is enabled by setting the DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_MODE environment variable to the value setup when running the container. Additional environment variables are used to configure the setup logic:

* DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_USERNAME: The username to set for the system's initial super-user (Required).
* DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_PASSWORD: The password to set for the system's inital super-user (Required).
* DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ORG: The name to set for the system's initial organization (Required).
* DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_BUCKET: The name to set for the system's initial bucket (Required).
* DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_RETENTION: The duration of the system's initial bucket should retain data. If not set, the initial bucket will retain data forever.
* DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ADMIN_TOKEN: The authentication token to associate with the system's initial super-user. If not set, a token will be auto generated by the system.

Automated setup will generate metadata files and CLI configurations. It's recommended to mount volumes at both paths to avoid losing data.

```
    docker run \
        --name influx-server \
        -d -p 8086:8086 \
        -v "$PWD"/data:/var/lib/influxdb \
        -v "$PWD"/config:/etc/influxdb \
        -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_MODE=setup \
        -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_USERNAME=my-user \
        -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_PASSWORD=my-password \
        -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_ORG=my-org \
        -e DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_BUCKET=my-bucket \
        mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux/base/influxdb:2
```

**NOTE:** Automated setup will not run if an existing `boltdb` file is found at the configured path. This behavior allows for the InfluxDB container to reboot post-setup without encountering `DB is already set up` errors.

## Usage

### Start an InfluxDB instance

    docker run --name influx-server -d -p 8086:8086 -v myInfluxVolume:/var/lib/influxdb mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux/base/influxdb:2

After starting the container you can use the web interface at http://localhost:8086/ to setup and customize your Influx database.

Find more about API Endpoints & Ports [here](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.6/reference/api/).

The default container startup command is `influxd`.

### Interacting with InfluxDB
Once an InfluxDB instance has completed the initial setup, its APIs will unlock. See the main documentation site for reference information and examples on:

* [Writing data](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.0/write-data/)
* [Reading data](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.0/query-data/)
* [Configuring security](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.0/security/)
* [And more!](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.0/)

#### Example of writing data using Influx CLI that comes with the image
There are multiple ways to write and query data for InfluxDB, one way is using InfluxDB UI, Influx CLI and InfluxDB API. The docker image comes together with Influx CLI.

```
docker exec influx-server influx write \
	--org my-org \
	--bucket my-bucket \
	--precision s "
home,room=Living\ Room temp=21.1,hum=35.9,co=0i 1641024000
home,room=Kitchen temp=21.0,hum=35.9,co=0i 1641024000
home,room=Living\ Room temp=21.4,hum=35.9,co=0i 1641027600
home,room=Kitchen temp=23.0,hum=36.2,co=0i 1641027600
home,room=Living\ Room temp=21.8,hum=36.0,co=0i 1641031200
home,room=Kitchen temp=22.7,hum=36.1,co=0i 1641031200
home,room=Living\ Room temp=22.2,hum=36.0,co=0i 1641034800
home,room=Kitchen temp=22.4,hum=36.0,co=0i 1641034800
"
```

**NOTE:** This is assuming that you setup your database following the [`Automated Database Setup`](#automated-database-setup).

#### Example of quering data using Influx CLI that comes with the image
This is an example of quering for the data we wrote in section [`Example of writing data using Influx CLI that comes with the image`](#example-of-writing-data-using-influx-cli-that-comes-with-the-image) using [Flux query](https://docs.influxdata.com/influxdb/v2.6/get-started/query/?t=influx+CLI#query-data-with-flux).

```
docker exec influx-server influx query '
from(bucket: "my-bucket")
	|> range(start: 2022-01-01T08:00:00Z, stop: 2022-01-01T20:00:01Z)
	|> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "home")
	|> filter(fn: (r) => r._field== "co" or r._field == "hum" or r._field == "temp")
'
```

**NOTE:** This is assuming that you setup your database following the [`Automated Database Setup`](#automated-database-setup).

### Launch Azure Linux shell

The InfluxDB image ships with a bash shell. The launch command can be provided to docker run command to Launch Azure Linux shell. The following command will launch the shell:

    docker run -it --rm mcr.microsoft.com/azurelinux/base/influxdb:2 /bin/bash
